stances.claim: To honor the 14 bar exam toppers and passers of FLP, CJP hosted an 'asalto' in his home on Jan 11, exclusively for the 160 members of the FLP Society of Scholars (law scholars + MBA fellows + dissertation writing contest winners). To show appreciation for 6th placer Enrico Paguia, FLP gave him an additional P100,000 atop his P250,000 yearly scholarship grant.
stances.rhetorical_move: asalto + Society-of-Scholars triplet + Paguia-bonus anchoring opening

stances.claim: Every time the bar exam results are released, CJP is transported to his 1960 bar experience, recalled with empathy and compassion by his FEU law dean Jovito R. Salonga -- CJP's esteemed professor and guru, role model both in legal career and life.

In the Foreword of Salonga and Miranda-Feliciano's late-2007 'A Test of Courage,' Salonga wrote that CJP took the Bar Review seriously but was hospitalized during the first Sunday of the 1960 bar exams because of diarrhea and flu -- there was heavy downpour the night before, and CJP had to walk through flooded water on R. Papa Street connecting FEU Hospital (where he was confined) and the University of the East (the venue). Discouraged by his first-day performance, CJP came asking for advice; after shaking and holding hands a little longer than usual, Salonga said 'Art, take the exams, you will get well' -- CJP followed the advice and placed 6th in the 1960 bar exams.
stances.rhetorical_move: Salonga-Foreword verbatim reproduction + hand-shaking + Art-take-the-exams pep-talk + 6th-place outcome

stances.claim: Dean Salonga -- one of the brightest legal minds and a most revered Senate president, joint Numero Uno (tied with Jose W. Diokno) in the 1944 bar exam -- is one of the few in the world to finish a Master of Laws at Harvard and a doctorate at Yale. Those who have read CJP's decisions and writing will surely detect Salonga's legal philosophy and life values; CJP tries to echo, even if unworthily and faintly, Salonga's teaching that law cannot be separated from life and should be used as a brick in building the social edifice and as a means to fulfill the deepest aspirations of man.
stances.rhetorical_move: Salonga credentials-roster + Harvard-LLM-Yale-doctorate rare-combination + echo-unworthily-and-faintly framing

stances.claim: Sixty-six years later, CJP remains in the privileged but humble position of being able to pay forward the kindness and guidance once received -- through FLP, CJP has had the honor of supporting some of the nation's most promising law students. As none of CJP's children or grandchildren has pursued the legal profession, it has been a special joy not only to support but also to journey with the young law scholars.

What lies beyond the bar tests is a crucial question new lawyers must confront -- how they uphold integrity, competence, and trustworthiness will be judged by time. In CJP's Monday column, he humbly expressed his hope that more lawyers will devote their lives and careers not only to competence but also to ethics; the CPRA reminds us that 'an ethical lawyer is a lawyer possessed of integrity, the sum of all the ethical values that every lawyer must embody and exhibit. A lawyer with integrity, therefore, acts with independence, propriety, fidelity, competence and diligence, equality and accountability.' When these traits are ignored, people lose faith in the nobility of our profession and in the efficacy of the rule of law.

'God is not finished with him yet,' exhorted Salonga in his Preface to CJP's first book (1994), 'Love God, Serve Man' -- perhaps that was Salonga's way of encouraging CJP to continue the spiritual journey that seeks to transform more lives as Salonga did with CJP's; while competence may already be evident in our law scholars, integrity and independence must be lived out amid temptation and pressure. CJP hopes they too will find a mentor or a figure in history to emulate and inspire them.
stances.rhetorical_move: Salonga God-is-not-finished verbatim Preface citation + transform-more-lives mentorship-extension

stances.claim: In the Foreword to CJP's 2006 'Liberty and Prosperity,' Salonga remarked that CJP had overemphasized his role -- 'In a deeper sense, Art is my mentor. For he is no longer the same person I used to know.' With gratitude and discernment, CJP now fully grasps the depth and breadth of that statement; it resonates with CJP as he hopes someday to enjoy the honor of saying those words to some of his scholars who would have risen and surpassed his life and career -- 'truly fulfilled, elevated, and levitated.'

To the FLP law scholars whom CJP considers his successors -- wherever their legal careers may take them, savor the fruits of hard work, and please continue to uphold the rule of law with clarity, courage, and integrity. May they safeguard the liberty of our people and help them overcome poverty and nurture prosperity under the rule of law.
stances.rhetorical_move: considers-his-successors mentorship-anointing + clarity-courage-integrity triplet + signature-philosophy closing

one_paragraph_summary: After hosting an asalto in his home for the 14 FLP bar topnotchers and passers, Panganiban reflects on his own 1960 bar experience as recounted in Salonga and Miranda-Feliciano's late-2007 'A Test of Courage': hospitalized with diarrhea and flu, wading through R. Papa Street floodwater between FEU Hospital and the University of the East, and pep-talked by Dean Salonga ('Art, take the exams, you will get well') into placing sixth. He honors Salonga -- joint Numero Uno with Diokno in the 1944 bar, Harvard LLM, Yale doctorate, and revered Senate President -- as the model he tries to echo. He stresses that what lies beyond the bar is a demanding ethics test under the CPRA's six-canon integrity formulation, that competence is measurable but ethics is not always apparent, and that new lawyers need a mentor or historical role model to emulate. He closes with the hope that someday his scholars will surpass him, fulfilling Salonga's 'God is not finished with him yet' promise.
